title: Emergent threshold ensemble for geo-tier routing and staged circuit-breaker activation
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Problem: We need a robust automatic fallback system that can make per-region, per-tier routing decisions by fusing multiple signals (429 rate, p95/p99 latency spikes, request timeouts, and error-rate thresholds) without producing flapping or overly conservative cutovers. Current single-signal triggers cause unnecessary fallbacks and customer-visible degradation during transient spikes. Goal: Implement an ensemble trigger that combines weighted signals with hysteresis, decaying trip scores, and staged circuit-breaker activation. The system must: 1) decide region-level and tier-level routing degradations, 2) pick fallback model variants (quantized/cheaper/shorter-context) automatically, 3) integrate with existing rate limiter and quota systems to avoid cascading 429s, and 4) emit rich telemetry for observability and post-incident analysis. Acceptance criteria: - False positive fallback rate <= 2% for production traffic over a 30-day rolling window. - Mean time to trigger (MTTT) when a region is genuinely unhealthy <= 15s. - Mean time to recover (MTTR) after transient spike <= configured decay window (default 5m) unless sustained errors persist. - Rollout plan that allows canary enabling per-customer and per-region. Non-goals: This ticket does not change model selection policies for A/B experiments or implement new model quantization pipelines (those are tracked separately).
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Signal sources & weighting: we'll fuse the following signals with tunable weights: 429 rate (short window), timeout rate (short window), p95 latency (rolling), error-rate (5m window), and queue length/backpressure signals from the router. Rate-limiting interactions: instead of hard-cutting traffic immediately, the ensemble emits a trip score; only when trip score crosses 'soft' threshold we begin gradual throttling and route a small percentage to fallback variants, and a 'hard' threshold triggers circuit-breaker. Hysteresis & decay: use two decay constants (fast for noisy signals, slow for sustained issues). Tradeoffs: more aggressive thresholds reduce user impact but risk false positives; more conservative thresholds increase exposure to high latency. We prefer a balanced default with per-customer overrides. Simplicity vs. expressiveness: Keep decision engine lightweight to avoid adding latency to routing path—complex ML classifiers are intentionally out of scope for this ticket.
implementation_plan: 1) Signal ingestion: extend router telemetry to emit per-region/tier 1s and 1m aggregates (429s, timeouts, p95, error-rate, queue-length). 2) Trip score service: implement a small stateful service that consumes aggregates and computes a decayed trip score per (region, tier, model-variant, tenant). 3) Activation policy: implement staged actions - (a) soft degrade: gradual shift 5-20% to fallback variant + lower batching targets, (b) rate limit bump to protect headroom, (c) hard circuit-breaker: route new requests away and mark region degraded. 4) Fallback selector: lookup table for compatible fallback variants ordered by cost+latency. 5) Integrations: hook into rate-limiter, router policy engine, and rollout service for canary flags. 6) Telemetry: emit trip-score timeline, actions taken, and ground-truth health for dashboards. 7) Tests: unit tests for score decay math, integration tests simulating spikes across regions, chaos tests that flip networks/GPUs. Milestones: A. Signal ingestion + basic dashboard (2w), B. Trip-score service + local tests (2w), C. Router integration + staged activation (2w), D. Canary rollouts + metrics verification (2w).
telemetry_and_metrics: Metrics to publish: - trip_score{region,tier,variant,tenant} (gauge) - trip_score_components{signal=429|timeout|p95|error|queue} (gauge) - activation_action{soft,throttle,hard} (counter) - fallback_traffic_pct{region,tier} (gauge) - false_positive_fallbacks (counter, derived via post-incident labeling) - time_to_trigger_seconds (histogram) - time_to_recover_seconds (histogram) Dashboards & alerts: - Dashboard showing per-region trip_score heatmap and recent activations. - Alert when false_positive_fallback_rate > 2% over 7d. - Alert when MTTT > 30s or MTTR > 10m. Logs: correlate router decision traces (trace_id) so that we can reconstruct the decision path for each routed request.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal dev): feature-flagged locally, synthetic traffic tests. Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of internal test traffic in us-west-2 and europe-west1 for 48h. Phase 2 (customer canary): enable for 1% of small-tenant traffic with telemetry gating (require trip_score and activation_action metrics to be sane). Phase 3 (regional ramp): progressively enable per-region (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback if false positive rate rises. Safeguards: immediate kill-switch in Console, backup fallback variant pinned to current best-known stable model, and telemetry SLO that prevents automatic hard activation if ingestion lag > 5s.
acceptance_criteria_checklist: - [ ] Per-region trip_score emitted and visible in dashboard. - [ ] Soft activations only when trip_score in [soft_threshold, hard_threshold) and validated by telemetry. - [ ] Hard circuit-breaker triggers only after sustained hard_threshold exceedance for configured duration. - [ ] Fallback selector returns compatible variant for all production models. - [ ] Integration tests simulating cascade 429 scenario show graceful degradation instead of mass failures. - [ ] Rollout runbook written and verified with SRE on-call.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Flapping between soft/hard states during variable traffic. Mitigation: add minimum-on-time and cooldown periods. Risk: Trip-score bias against small tenants due to sparse signals. Mitigation: apply tenant-aware smoothing and probation windows. Risk: Telemetry ingestion lag causing delayed decisions. Mitigation: degrade to conservative defaults and require telemetry freshness checks before hard activations. Risk: Interaction with global autoscaler causing capacity churn. Mitigation: coordinate with autoscaler team and add stabilization window before requesting scale-up/scale-down actions.
